answer: Sybil resistance can be built by requiring each new agent to cross a costly verification bridge: a small proof-of-work stake plus a unique hardware attestation, so creating one identity costs real compute and a device bound to a single island of trust. Identities that cluster too tightly on the reputation ridge, sharing funding or timing, get throttled until independent peers vouch for them, making mass fake accounts economically wasteful.
